instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
cards.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your verdict on my audition was 'interesting.' I'm returning it for more detail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I'm trying to be encouraging.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Encouragement is permitted. Omissions aren't. Give me the half you swallowed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your singing was better than your dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That comparison isn't approved as a complete answer. Tell me whether I'm booking dance lessons or asking for a number I can sing standing still.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't approved these minutes. 'Discussion of my proposal' leaves out what happened to my name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sign them and we can eat. Nobody wanted an awkward record.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dinner is deferred. Who is 'nobody'? Name the person who wanted me out of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. I suggested someone else present, to save your proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That admission is noted. The minutes stay unsigned until you name the replacement too. I won't approve appointing 'someone else' to present my work.

cards.title: Hope with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into believing that the outcome can still change, even when the evidence is thin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved another attempt at our parade route. Two streets refused us; the whole town hasn't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The only route left goes behind the supermarket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then that's the route we're considering. Take the other pencil and show me where people could cheer by the loading bay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My dad would come. He works there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first spectator is approved. Put him on the map, then help me find a place for a second. You can see a parade there now, can't you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've authorized a little preparation for our cafe. Help me choose the glasses for our first celebration.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're only on the waiting list. I haven't told Mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may keep it between us. For now, give me your recommendation: which glasses would belong on our tables?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: These two. Mum would insist on a mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Recommendation approved, with one addition: choose her mug. You've just put a customer in the cafe with us. Let's keep that seat for her.

cards.title: Say the Scary Part
cards.instruction: Get someone else to name the frightening possibility or vulnerable feeling before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I won't open the landlord's letter until you've given me the worst-case report for our shop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've only missed one payment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The count is accepted. You have permission to say the consequence we're frightened of.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could lose the shop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now give me the personal part. Dad trusted me with it; what would losing it make me in his eyes? I'm assigning you that sentence first too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we skate this qualifier, I'm giving you the first word on the possibility we've been avoiding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want you carrying that onto the ice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That concern is noted. I'm already carrying it; you're authorized to say it aloud before I do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We might not qualify. I'd still want to skate with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep going. That second sentence mattered more than the first. Tell me what I was afraid you would do if we failed; I want you to name it before me.

cards.title: See What This Took
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought the angry draft of my apology. You may appreciate how much of it I didn't send.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I appreciated the apology. Why bring this?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because saying sorry took ten minutes. Keeping the rest from you took all night, and that effort deserves recognition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now I want to read what you kept from me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Reading isn't approved. You may admire the thickness with it closed. I'd like you to recognize my restraint without making me exercise it all over breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I told the committee I couldn't chair another year. Please appreciate what those two sentences took.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. Could you stay on until we find someone?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I rehearsed in your car until I stopped apologising. That wasn't me advertising a temporary vacancy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll tell them you're exhausted and need a break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't supply the excuse I spent an hour removing. Could you recognise a refusal I finally managed without one?

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Choose What Matters More
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're calling your audition number. I'm clearing the way in; are you choosing the part or a safe ride home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want the part. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may choose either route. I won't approve pretending that walking in comes with control of their faces.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The escort is approved. That promise isn't. I'll stay with you, but you must choose whether the part is worth being heard. Shall I take you in or home?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I approve renewing our lease, choose whether you want my honest answer about living together or a peaceful dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your honest answer. Just don't say anything that makes me panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I won't approve those as one request. You may have my answer, or we can order and leave it alone tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Answer. But start by saying we're fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That preface is not approved. It tells me what answer you're willing to hear. Do you want my real one enough to let me begin without it?
